meta.title: Super zoo store CS314 — brand-level shopper profiles (real pilot data)
meta.store: CS314 (Kozomín), single store of a ~200-store chain — NOT generalisable to the chain
meta.window: POS 2026-07-07 to 2026-08-04 (28 daily files; 2026-07-08 file absent). Peak tick/cottage season. Ontario/3+1 screen creatives ran from 2026-07-27/28.

sources.pos_lines: mm-business/clients/superzoo/POS data/raw POS data/POS_2026-07-07.xlsx … POS_2026-08-04.xlsx (13,153 lines, 4,738 receipts, 2,058,957 CZK gross)
sources.personas: mm-business/clients/superzoo/POS data/persona_scoring_full_export.csv (15,041 person_ids; source build 3,150 / recovered_local 11,891)

join_keys.pos_line_to_receipt: (Work Station ID, POS Receipt No_). Each key maps to exactly one End Date and Time and one daily file.
join_keys.receipt_to_visitor: pos_link_export (workstation, receipt_no) -> person_id. 0 duplicate keys; receipt_no alone is also unique in this window, BUT till 2's counter rolls over 99999 -> 20 on 2026-07-28 (between 14:09 and 15:19), so always key on workstation + receipt_no, and add the POS date for windows longer than one counter cycle.
join_keys.identity_note: person_id is VISIT-level: every person_id claims exactly one receipt (7,815 ids / 7,815 receipts). 'Distinct shoppers' therefore = distinct shopper-visits; repeat customers cannot be de-duplicated and between-visit brand switching cannot be observed.

confidence_threshold.rationale: confidence = winning candidate's share of match weight. >=0.3 keeps matches clearly above the ~0.25 chance level at the median 3-4 candidates (2,385 receipts, 50.6%). >=0.5 is the delivered-report 'high-confidence' convention (1,234, 26.2%) but effectively keeps only quiet-till moments (median 2 candidates). >=0.0 = every persona-tagged match (3,229). Subsets are nested, so agreement across thresholds shows a signal survives stricter matching (mis-matching attenuates persona differences toward 100) — it is not independent replication.

meta.suppression_rule: Any cell (persona x group, category/time x group, group total) with fewer than 25 distinct shopper-visits is suppressed ('<25'); for suppressed persona cells only the direction vs base is kept ('direction_only').

base_definitions.petfood_shoppers: matched receipts containing >=1 dog or cat Krmivo line (dry, wet, treats, supplements)
base_definitions.all_matched: all matched receipts at the threshold

meta.index: 100 x (persona share in group) / (persona share among matched pet-food shoppers). p_vs_rest = two-proportion z-test, group vs all other matched receipts.
meta.multiple_testing_warning: ~300 persona/time/category tests were run; ~15 would pass p<0.05 by chance. Use the robustness grades in key_findings, not single p-values.
meta.receipt_level_metrics_note: basket, category attach, dog/cat and time-of-day blocks use ALL 4,712 receipts (no visitor match needed); persona blocks use matched receipts only.

not_computed.premium_tier_within_third_party: NOT COMPUTED — 'premium third-party' = all attributed third-party brands in the category (channel carries only premium/super-premium; mass brands absent). No SKU price-tier classification.
not_computed.per_weekday_profiles: NOT COMPUTED — only weekend vs weekday and four hour bands.
not_computed.price_per_kg_significance: NOT COMPUTED — price-per-kg figures are descriptive.

attribution.method: Controlled vocabulary over Czech product names (Název CZ), first match wins; VAFO rules precede own-brand rules. Own = Plaček house brands (founder roster + typo fixes + Mr. Dental, Let's Play, BeFUN). Beaphar and Avicentra = third-party per facts.yaml (NB targets.yaml still lists Avicentra as own — conflict). Non-brandable = live animals/feed insects/plants (Živé), store items (Prodejny), unclassified rows, rounding, charity, vouchers, carrier bags. No pre-existing attribution script or roster file was found in mm-business or analysis-api; the vocabulary was rebuilt and validated.

third_party_czk.note: our wider third-party lexicon attributes more of the facts.yaml residual (unattributed 4.3% vs 7.6%)

attribution.item_prefix_crosscheck: Item-number prefixes behave as supplier codes and corroborate the name lexicon (294/293 = VAFO, 213/214 = Ontario, 45x = Plaček accessory brands, G1x = Trixie, A1 = Tetra, L3/L4 = N&D).

Suburban Women in their 30s.definition: Homemaker / 'soccer mom' / dress; biggest segment (~24% of sessions)

Young Women in their 20s.definition: Urban dweller, minimalist casual, young professional

Young Men in Bright Casuals.definition: Polo shirt, paw-print graphic, bright fabric

Students in their Teens.definition: After-school errand, youth casual, college student

VAFO_total.definition: Any VAFO line (Brit, Brit Care, Brit Premium, Brit Fresh, Carnilove)

Brit_all.definition: Any Brit-branded line (Brit Care, Brit Premium by Nature, Brit Fresh, other Brit)

Ontario_cat_food.definition: Ontario line in cat food (any cat Krmivo)

Magic_Litter_Pearls.definition: Magic Litter or Magic Pearls line

Spectrum.definition: Any Spectrum Brands line (Tetra, Eukanuba, IAMS, 8in1, FURminator)

Brit_not_Ontario.definition: Brit line and no Ontario line

Ontario_not_Brit.definition: Ontario line and no Brit line

Brit_and_Ontario.definition: Brit AND Ontario in the same basket

dry_dog_mixed.definition: Dry dog food: third-party AND own in same basket

cat_food_mixed.definition: Cat meal: third-party AND own in same basket

food_mixer_any.definition: Any food (dog/cat, incl. treats): third-party AND own-brand in same basket

VAFO_food_and_own_food.definition: VAFO food AND own-brand food in same basket

drydog_price_per_kg_paid.note: CZK actually paid per kg = receipt line amount / (qty x pack kg parsed from the name). Cells from <25 lines suppressed.

key_findings.finding: Brit and Ontario shoppers have the same persona mix: no persona differs by more than 3.5pp (all p>=0.21; n=322 vs 482 at >=0.3). Same at >=0.5 and >=0.0.

130 of 627 Brit baskets (20.7%) also hold Ontario; 60 of those 130 (46%) hold Ontario ONLY as treats, 39 are 'Brit meal + Ontario treat'. Brit dry and Ontario dry dog food almost never share a basket: fewer than 25 of the 203 Brit-dry baskets in 28 days (suppressed cell), against 130 Brit+Ontario co-baskets overall. Co-baskets are multi-pet (25.4% dog+cat vs 9.5%) and the biggest (761 CZK vs 540).

Dry dog food is a one-brand trip: fewer than 25 of 605 dry-dog baskets (<4.1%) hold more than one dry-food brand at all, own + third-party mixes included. Cat meals are assembled: 89 of 546 (16.3%) mix own + third-party, 160 (29.3%) hold >1 brand.
Dog Fantasy (own) skews Young Women 20s (25.4%, index 139, p=0.005; 144 at >=0.5; 131 at >=0.0) and repels Suburban Men 40s (13.8%, index 70, p=0.008). Trixie draws Men 40s at par (19.9%, index 101).
Magic Litter/Magic Pearls buyers: Young Women 20s 26.7% (index 145, p=0.013; 144 p=0.004 at >=0.0); Suburban Women 30s only 25.2% (index 75). Under-30 roll-up 40.7% (index 134, p=0.011).

Suburban Men 40s over-index on dry dog food whichever brand (third-party-only 29.0%, index 146, p=0.010; own-only 26.8%, index 135, p=0.026; both hold at >=0.0) but buy no bigger sacks (mean pack 5.4 kg, 28% >=10 kg vs Suburban Women 30s 5.9 kg, 32%).

Brit dog food over-indexes Young Women 20s (23.6%, index 129, p=0.038; Brit overall 135 p=0.013 before the 27 Jul Ontario creatives) and Men 40s (24.5%, index 124; 142 p=0.041 at >=0.5); Suburban Women 30s, the store's largest persona, under-index (27.5%, index 82).

Retirees are the brand-mixers: 33.3% of their food baskets hold own + third-party food vs 21.6% for everyone else (p=0.014; index 149 among mixers). Suburban Men 40s mix least (17.1% vs 23.6%, p=0.025).
Men 40s avoid third-party cat meals: 14.5% of third-party cat-meal shoppers (index 73, p=0.043; 71 p=0.016 at >=0.0).

Big-sack (>=10 kg) CZK/kg actually paid: Brit Premium by Nature 56.4 (40 lines), Rasco Premium 58.2 (41), Brit Care 103.3 (26), Ontario 107.6 (52). Ontario is priced at Brit Care, not under Brit; Rasco Premium is Brit Premium's real own-brand shadow. (Elbeville all pack sizes 173.5 CZK/kg, 35 lines — the priciest own-brand dog food.)

Third-party-only dry dog baskets over-index after 18:00 (21.7% vs 16.7%, p=0.042); Ontario dog-food baskets under-index after 18:00 (14.2% vs 18.1%, p=0.029); own-only dry dog under-indexes before noon (23.1% vs 28.5%, p=0.039).
Spectrum (in this store = Tetra/aquarium): Suburban Men 40s are 31.0% of buyers (index 157, p=0.012; 138 p=0.048 at >=0.0); 19.5% of Spectrum baskets also carry live fish/feed insects.
Suburban Women 30s, the largest persona (33.6% of pet-food shoppers), have the smallest baskets: 483 CZK vs 539 (p=0.011; 457 p=0.036 at >=0.5; 500 p=0.028 at >=0.0).

The July 10-day pilot gradient (young personas -> house brands, older -> VAFO) does NOT replicate on 28 days: own-brand share of attributed spend is 47% (Young Women 20s, CI 41-54) to 58% (Retirees, CI 46-71) with overlapping intervals.

thin_or_suppressed.Carnilove: 148 receipts; persona: only Suburban Women 30s passes (39.2%, index 117, n.s.); suppressed at >=0.5.
thin_or_suppressed.Elbeville: 61 receipts (982 CZK basket, 44.3% weekend p=0.03) — persona cells all <25.
thin_or_suppressed.Eukanuba_IAMS: Eukanuba 2,059 CZK, IAMS none — Spectrum here is Tetra/aquarium; no pet-food read possible.
thin_or_suppressed.small_own_brands: Let's Play/BeFUN (<25 receipts), Aqua Excellent, Active Dog, Mr. Dental/Dentosaurus, Repti Planet, Prospera Plus: persona cells <25 at >=0.3.
thin_or_suppressed.small_personas: Students (2.4% of pet-food shoppers), Young Men in Bright Casuals (3.9%), Active Young Adults (5.9%), Retirees (6.2%) fall below 25 in almost every brand cell; any brand card naming them (except Retirees x food-mixing / Ontario / own total) would need mock top-up.
thin_or_suppressed.strict_threshold: At >=0.5 most brand x persona cells fall below 25 — only Dog Fantasy (YW20), Brit dog food (SM40, YW20), Ontario (SW30, YW20, SM40, BCLA), Trixie (SW30, YW20) and the big category splits survive.
thin_or_suppressed.no_loyalty_id: Visit-level IDs only: 'switchers' across visits cannot be measured; 'mixers' = same-basket co-purchase.
